messages:
ishaan: quick idea — tie SIEM export TTLs to our evidence-hold system so exports auto-extend when a ticket hits legal/IR, otherwise expire to cheaper cold storage after X days :thinking_face:
kelly: sounds promising. how do you see RBAC working? we should avoid granting broad read perms to long-lived service accounts
ishaan: two parts: 1) ephemeral export service account (short-lived tokens via iam:impersonate + auditable creation), 2) per-export CMK envelope wrap. if ticket enters hold, orchestrator calls KMS.rewrap -> rotate key material and bump TTL on the object
anna: rewrap on hold makes sense. do we have a flow for emergency breakglass where SRE/IR need immediate access but still audited?
mike: also need to consider downstream SIEM consumers (splunk/elastic). They can't handle keywraps directly unless we unwrap before forwarding. that adds a vault/unwrap proxy step
ishaan: correct — plan is: forwarder -> unwrap-proxy (running in restricted VPC, IAM-protected) -> SIEM. unwrap-proxy only accepts short-lived certs minted per-export. every unwrap call logs to audit stream and CloudTrail
kelly: can you sketch the minimal IAM policy for the ephemeral SA? want to avoid full logs/* read perms
ishaan: example below (super minimal):
```
- resource: projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/export-ephemeral@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  allow: ["iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken", "kms.decrypt", "storage.objects.create"]
  condition: request.time < resource.expiry
```
anna: where does the evidence hold signal come from? JIRA webhook -> orchestration lambda?
ishaan: yes, Jira/IR system posts webhook to orchestration service which: 1) marks GCS/S3 objects as "hold", 2) calls KMS.rewrap if needed, 3) increments TTL on the export metadata store. we capture the correlation id: infra.export_id -> incident_id
mike: what's the fallback if the unwrap-proxy is unavailable (region outage)? we should have a degraded read path for high-severity incidents
ishaan: fallback policy: if unwrap-proxy unreachable, orchestrator will temporarily generate a one-time signed URL (timeboxed, rotated CMK) and notify oncall + IR channel. access requires 2-person approval via Ops ticket system. all actions logged
kelly: approvals and 2-person rule are good. just flagging the audit retention: we need to keep unwrap logs for at least 1 year for forensics
security-bot: [alert] note: creating service accounts with broad kms.decrypt permission will trigger compliance rule CMP-7; ensure you submit an exception request if needed
anna: thanks @security-bot. ishaan, what about export lifecycle costs? auto-expire to cold after 30d by default?
ishaan: default: 7d hot -> 30d warm -> 365d cold-archive. evidence-hold can pin to cold-archive with extended retention. we keep small indexable metadata for search outside of archive
mike: operational question: how do we rotate the per-export CMK? KMS has key rotation but per-export keys are envelope keys stored encrypted by a master CMK
ishaan: envelope keys are generated per-export and encrypted with project CMK. rotate master CMK every 90 days; per-export envelope keys can be rewrapped by calling KMS.rewrap to a new master if needed (e.g., hold escalation).
kelly: ok please add the following to the RFC: - minimal IAM policy, - unwrap-proxy runbook (restart/DR), - 2-person emergency access flow + audit retention spec, - cost model for tiering
ishaan: will draft RFC and link INF-2345. quick proof-of-concept commands:
```
# mint short-lived token
gcloud iam service-accounts signJwt export-ephemeral@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --payload='{"exp": "$(date -d "+10 minutes" +%s)"}'

# rewrap envelope key
gcloud kms keys versions rewrap --location=global --keyring=exports --key=master-cmk --ciphertext=ENC_BLOB
```
anna: love the PoC. can you post a flow diagram in the RFC showing where audit logs land (splunk vs. internal long-term archive)?
ishaan: yup — will include: audit -> bifurcate to splunk (30d index) + bucketed archive (365d) with object metadata linking back to incident id
mike: one more: let's ensure token exchange and unwrap-proxy metrics feed into console so we can set SLOs (latency/error) for unwrap path
kelly: agree. also add a playbook snippet for incident response that uses the timeboxed signed URL fallback and documents approvals
ishaan: ack. I'll open RFC today and ping this thread when ready. tagging: @kelly @anna @mike for review :white_check_mark:
